channel.title: The Local France - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local France (thelocal.fr)

item.title: How to watch the 2026 Winter Olympics on French TV
item.description: A year and a half after the Paris 2024 Olympics Games, how can sports fans in France catch all the action from the Winter Olympics in Milano Cortina, Italy?

item.title: 'Most people confessed': How to get points back on your French driver's license
item.description: France offers a special course to drivers who are at risk of losing their licence - which aims to get drivers to change their risky driving behaviour, with the added bonus of getting back points on the driving licence.

item.title: 'A ritual shaped by an industry' - The rise of the pricey Paris proposals
item.description: It's long had a reputation as the city of romance, but now the French capital is supporting a growing number of businesses that will arrange an extravagant marriage proposal in a landmark setting - for a hefty fee, of course.

item.title: France bets on nuclear power to phase out fossil fuels
item.description: France's government on Thursday presented an energy plan to use less imported fossil fuels, including by ramping up nuclear-fuelled power production over the next decade.

item.title: Two Louvre staff arrested over ticket fraud
item.description: French police have dismantled a "large-scale" ticket fraud network at the Louvre in Paris, the museum said Thursday, while a source following the case said two staff had been arrested.

item.title: France's ex-minister Retailleau to run for president
item.description: A former interior minister of France who heads the country's right-wing Les Républicains party, Bruno Retailleau, announced on Thursday he will run in the 2027 presidential election, in a message shared with his party members seen by AFP.

item.title: ANALYSIS: Who's who in France's 2027 presidential election race
item.description: It's still more than a year away but it's already shaping up to be a seismic race for France - in April and May 2027, French people will go to the polls and pick their next president. Here's how the race is shaping up so far.

item.title: PODCAST: Le Pen faces the end and why France wants less meat but more babies
item.description: Welcome back to Talking France - this week's podcast covers the latest on the Le Pen trial, the ins and outs of private beaches in France and why the French government wants people to have more babies but eat less meat.

item.title: Friday the 13th: The most unusual French superstitions
item.description: Unlike some countries, Friday the 13th is regarded as particularly lucky in France - but that doesn't mean there aren't plenty of other superstitions about things that will allegedly bring you bad fortune.

item.title: La Belle Vie: Why France wants more babies and what love looks like in Paris
item.description: From France wanting women to have more babies and what Valentine's Day looks like for the French, this week’s La Belle Vie newsletter offers an essential starting point for eating, talking, drinking, and living like a local.
